candidates.title: HAS_CAPACITY_ENTITLEMENT_IN
candidates.definition: A named company has an explicitly stated present entitlement to an identified share or amount of production capacity associated with another named company. The underlying facility may be planned; the entitlement itself must be stated as present.
candidates.direction: beneficiary Company -> company associated with the disclosed capacity (Company)

recurrence.limit: Repeated disclosure of one project; not two independent rights or cross-issuer validation.

existing_alternatives: OWNS: equity ownership does not encode a capacity right
CONTRACTS_MANUFACTURING_TO: a manufacturing engagement does not encode entitlement
DEPENDS_ON: dependence is neither implied nor stated
Ownership percentage qualifier: same numeric value need not mean same legal right
exclusions: No edge from equity ownership alone
No current manufacturing activity inferred from entitlement to a planned facility
No commitment or investment treated as production capacity
No share inferred from ownership percentage
competency_questions: Which companies have explicitly disclosed production-capacity entitlements, at which named company, and in what source?
Does a 10% ownership stake establish a separate 10% capacity right?
candidates.evaluation: Directed relation tuple; source entailment independently scored; percentage and planned-production context retained separately.
candidates.review_question: Is this a reusable directed relationship, a qualifier on an existing fact, or an unnecessary concept? Identify the existing predicate if it already captures the capacity-right meaning.

candidates.title: Facility / OPERATES_FACILITY / LOCATED_IN
candidates.definition: An explicitly identified physical operating site, distinct from its owning organization and geographic location.
candidates.direction: OPERATES_FACILITY: Company -> Facility; LOCATED_IN: Facility -> Geography

recurrence.limit: Repeated four-site disclosure; no independent multi-issuer support.

existing_alternatives: OPERATES_IN preserves geography but loses the site identity
Company is an organization, not its factory
Product and Technology are not physical sites
exclusions: Facility class definition alone does not establish an instance
Table headings alone do not establish operation
Plans to build a site do not establish current operation
Ownership is not inferred from operation
competency_questions: Which explicitly identified facility is operated by a company, and where is that facility located?
candidates.evaluation: Blocked until the naming/identity rule is resolved. Require a source designation, or explicitly approve issuer-scoped descriptive site identity applied equally to both conditions.
candidates.review_question: Do these location-qualified site descriptions identify facility instances under the frozen naming rule? If not, reject these positive examples and request named-site evidence.

candidates.title: CUSTOMER_BASE_CONCENTRATED_IN
candidates.definition: A company-level customer-base fact explicitly says its customer base is concentrated in specified geographies. It does not identify individual customers or their revenue shares.
candidates.direction: Attribute of issuer customer-base scope; geography values, not customer-company edges.
existing_alternatives: OPERATES_IN concerns the issuer, not the geography of its customer base
EXPOSED_TO does not encode concentration scope precisely
exclusions: Do not create unnamed customer entities
Do not infer geographic concentration from operating sites
Do not infer a revenue percentage
candidates.evaluation: Separate scoped-attribute task; current six-field relation adapter cannot encode this qualifier.
candidates.review_question: Specify a supported base fact and its owner before approving the qualifier. Is a company-scoped attribute contract sufficient?

candidates.title: DEVELOPMENT_DISCONTINUED
candidates.definition: The source explicitly states that development of an identified program or technology was discontinued.
candidates.direction: Lifecycle state of an evidenced development fact; not a positive current DEVELOPS assertion.
existing_alternatives: Existing audited claim supersession/retraction may already preserve this information
A generic time qualifier does not state discontinuation by itself
exclusions: Do not infer an exact stop date
Do not turn an absence in a later filing into discontinuation
Do not keep a stopped program as current development
candidates.evaluation: Separate lifecycle task; do not claim additional current-positive relation recall.
candidates.review_question: Does existing lifecycle machinery represent this without a schema addition? Is the program sufficiently identified?

new_predicate_origin: New development search, not an earlier reviewer-approved proposal
